intro: Professionals and everyday users convert horsepower (hp) (hp) to kilowatts (kW) when working across imperial and metric standards in automotive engine output ratings, electric motor sizing, solar inverter specifications, and appliance load planning. One horsepower (mechanical) equals 0.7457 kilowatts, while 1 kilowatt equals 1.341022 horsepower (hp). Whether you are verifying power specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Exact NIST Factor vs. Early Rounding Drift
items: The exact conversion factor from Horsepower (Mechanical) to Kilowatt is 0.74569987, derived from the 1959 International Yard and Pound Agreement (1 inch = 25.4 mm, 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg).

In structural engineering, CNC machining, or bulk inventory totals, rounding the multiplier to 2 decimal places too early can introduce cumulative tolerance errors; always compute with the full factor and round only the final displayed figure.

faqs.question: How many kilowatts (kW) are in 1 horsepower (mechanical) (hp)?
faqs.answer: There are 0.74569987 kilowatts (kW) in 1 horsepower (mechanical) (hp), which rounds to 0.7457 kW for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 kilowatt equals 1.341022 horsepower (hp).

faqs.question: How do I convert horsepower (hp) to kilowatts (hp to kW)?
faqs.answer: To convert horsepower (hp) to kilowatts, use the formula: kW = hp × 0.74569987. For example, converting 50 hp gives 37.285 kW.

faqs.question: What is 50 horsepower (hp) in kilowatts?
faqs.answer: 50 horsepower (hp) (hp) equals exactly 37.285 kilowatts (kW) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
